heading: The Dual-Agent Talker-Reasoner Architecture
content: Also implemented as the Librarian/Query Agent and Sandbox Executor pattern. Addresses context bloat and the lost-in-the-middle problem by decoupling memory tracking from task execution. The Executor Agent (the Sandbox) has zero historical context bloat, spun up with a narrow constrained context window optimized exclusively for one immediate subtask or code execution, keeping reasoning efficiency high, token costs low, and avoiding instruction dilution. The Query/Talker Agent (the Memory Layer) manages long-term cross-session memory, handling active user prompts, semantic search, and historical retrieval. Stops context bloat via three steps: isolated turn execution (Query Agent searches a persistent storage layer like Mem0 or Memori and isolates a micro-payload), stateless passing (the micro-payload goes to the Executor Agent), and wiping the slate (once the Executor finishes, it returns output and its sandbox resets). This pattern is attributed to Marktechpost and top AI labs coverage per the source chat, but should be treated as a named pattern circulating in AI-engineering blog content, not one canonical spec.

heading: MiMo Code + Mem0
content: MiMo Code, released by Xiaomi's AI team per the source (early June 2026), is a MIT-licensed, terminal-native, long-horizon AI coding harness, an open-source fork of the OpenCode engine written in TypeScript, at github.com/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code. Claimed to handle 200-plus execution-step tasks without context choking (unverified vendor/blogger claim) via a dual-layer setup: the MiMo-V2-Flash/Pro foundation engine is a context-lean sandbox executor wiping its short-term workspace constantly, while a master orchestration/memory layer feeds it micro-payloads and tracks broader engineering goals. Mem0 (formerly Embedchain), at github.com/mem0ai/mem0, is the memory engine commonly paired with this pattern: it extracts facts and updates a graph/vector layer dynamically (often via Neo4j), letting a Query Agent pull only the precise memory vectors needed for the next step. Reverse-engineering targets inside MiMo-Code per the source: packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/ for multi-agent orchestration/sub-agent dispatch logic; files implementing /dream, /distill, /goal routines for compressing noisy terminal execution loops into permanent memory (with /dream running async between sessions as a cleanup pass, a good template for a cron-style JSONL cleanup job); and discover/registry sandboxing files for directory-permission/file-system boundary checks, useful for a Red Agent auditor layer. Local install for testing: curl -fsSL https://mimo.xiaomi.com/install | bash (Mac/Linux) or npm install -g @mimo-ai/cli (Windows). Exact file paths are as stated in the source conversation, not independently confirmed against the live repo.

heading: The User's Real Hardware Topology
content: A three-device private neural mesh connected via Tailscale P2P. Motorola Razr Ultra 25 (mobile orchestrator/STT router, the daily driver) runs Qwen 3.5 9B (Q4_0 GGUF) plus OmniNeural-4B for persistent STT-to-meta-prompt transformation during Claude/Gemini sessions, deciding whether a request is answerable locally, needs a tool call, or should be shot to a cloud front-end. Jetson (Nano Super), the headless home hub, runs a cloud API fallback (e.g. Gemini Flash/GPT-4o mini) or a local high-quant SLM via vLLM if RAM allows, hosts the 500GB SSD with Open-Wiki/LLM-Wiki flattened JSONL data, runs OB1 for memory orchestration, and runs OmniRoute as the token-preserving API gateway. Dragon Wing Rubik Pi 3 (Thundercomm, Qualcomm Dragonwing QCS6490) is the headless display/desktop GUI plus vision model plus Red Agent auditor, budgeted at about 2GB out of 8GB total LPDDR4x RAM (2GB weights plus 1GB runtime/KV cache, 5GB reserved for OS/display/vision) -- this was corrected mid-conversation after the source initially assumed only 2GB total RAM and suggested unworkable 8B models; once the user corrected to 8GB total, the recommendation shifted to Gemma 4 E2B/E4B. When home, the phone tailscales into the home network forming one continuous neural mesh loop; away from home, the phone's on-device Qwen model just needs to know how to act, not carry heavy knowledge -- the heavier dual-agent memory layer only engages once connected to the home hub.

heading: The Three-Layer Agent Pipeline
content: Layer 1, the Inquisitor and Router, runs on the phone (Qwen 3.5 9B) acting strictly as a traffic controller, never reading raw docs or long logs: local STT becomes a structured Meta-Prompt JSON, then routing logic decides simple request (answer on-device), complex coding/file query (package intent as a lightweight MCP tool call), or cloud engine front-end (forward directly to Claude Code CLI or Gemini APIs). Layer 2, the Governed Continuity Memory, runs on the home hub via OB1 plus Tailscale: when connected home, the phone reaches Nate Jones' OB1 (Open Brain) infrastructure on the Jetson; the Jetson's 500GB SSD holds Open-Wiki-compiled JSONL; when Qwen requests info, OB1's MCP server intercepts, runs a localized vector-match/semantic query against the Obsidian graph/PDF vaults, and returns a precise context slice (about 2K tokens) rather than dumping the whole file system into the prompt. Layer 3, the Stateless Executor and Red Agent, is the sandbox plus guardrails: the heavy execution model on the Jetson runs in a transient environment, receives the Layer 2 context slice, calls the CLI or builds the script, outputs the result, and destroys its own chat history immediately; the Rubik Pi 3 acts as a Red Agent/Code Auditor, and before any generated script executes or returns to the phone it passes through the Rubik Pi for a secondary verification sweep on syntax, correctness, and guardrail matching.

heading: The Auditor Layer -- Detailed Architecture
content: The Rubik Pi 3 is an asynchronous gatekeeper, not a direct executor -- the Jetson compiles code/scripts but never runs them directly on the main filesystem, piping the proposed payload to the Auditor first. Verification pipeline: (1) interception -- every generated CLI script/code block is packaged into a structured JSON payload with intended_task, proposed_code, target_directory; (2) static analysis (deterministic step) -- before invoking any LLM, basic checks like Python ast parsing or standard linters catch blatant syntax errors; (3) the Red Agent audit (cognitive step) -- a small specialized model reviews the payload against a strict immutable system prompt focused on security boundaries, optimization, and logical validation; (4) gatekeeping -- approved payloads get an execute signal, failed payloads get an error_log JSON block appended and are returned to the Executor for correction. Lightweight runtimes considered: llama.cpp via a persistent server binary (ARM NEON-optimized) for lightweight local HTTP/JSON API; Llamafile as a single-file portable executable for stable long-running headless edge servers; vLLM with PagedAttention reserved specifically for the Jetson Nano (needs real CUDA cores/unified memory), not recommended for the Rubik Pi 3's constrained footprint.

heading: Auditor Model Candidates -- Corrected Across the Conversation
content: The model recommendation for the Rubik Pi 3 auditor role was corrected multiple times as RAM constraints were clarified. First pass (assumed generic small footprint, before any RAM number was given): Llama-3-8B-Instruct (Q4_K_M), Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (Q4_0/Q4_K_S), Granite-3.0-8B-Instruct. Second pass (assumed only 2GB total RAM, corrected down after the user objected an 8B model would crash a 2GB system): Qwen-2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct (about 1.1-1.2GB, best fit, code-syntax-trained), Phi-3.5-mini-instruct heavily quantized to Q2_K/Q3_K_S (about 1.6-1.9GB), Granite-3.0-Light-2B/1B variants. Third pass (corrected again once the user clarified the board actually has 8GB total RAM, about 3GB AI-layer budget): Qwen-2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct still fits at about 1.1-1.2GB; Phi-3.5-mini-instruct quantized to Q2_K/Q3_K_S at about 1.6-1.9GB; Google Gemma-2-2B-IT at about 1.6GB Q4_K_M. Final recommendation: Gemma 4 E2B or E4B, using Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE) for high intelligence density at small size -- Gemma 4 E2B (2.3B effective params) is about 1.4GB at Q4_K_M, Gemma 4 E4B (4.5B effective params) is about 2.8GB, pushing near the 3GB cap but claimed to punch like an old 15B-plus model (unverified benchmark claim from the source chat). Natively multimodal (text/image/audio in one model), which matters because the Rubik Pi 3 is simultaneously the desktop vision model -- no separate CLIP/vision encoder needed alongside the text auditor model. Has day-one native llama.cpp GGUF support per the source.

heading: Token Preservation and Context Slicing -- OmniRoute + Open-Wiki
content: OmniRoute runs on the Jetson Nano as the core traffic gateway between the local network and the external web, routing across a claimed 230-plus API endpoints per the source (unverified endpoint count and unverified 75 percent token reduction figure, both from the source chat's citations), automatically routing heavy coding requests to a free high-tier cloud provider, and stripping repetitive/bloated system context headers from incoming streams to preserve free-tier token budgets during large project builds. Site referenced: omniroute.online. This is the same OmniRoute project already in this session's repo scope -- the source material's marketing framing (billions of free tokens monthly, 160-plus AI models) should be checked against OmniRoute's own docs/CLAUDE.md rather than taken from this Gemini citation. Open-Wiki holds the flattened Obsidian MD graphs, PDFs, and codebase schemas on the Jetson's 500GB SSD, compiled into JSONL; when a task triggers, Open-Wiki pulls a specific compressed JSONL context payload rather than uploading whole folders to the cloud model.

heading: Network Architecture: Tailscale P2P Mesh + WebSocket Protocol
content: All three devices run Tailscale, forming a secure encrypted overlay network (100.x.y.z address range) with direct device-to-device communication and no port-forwarding/public IP exposure. Illustrative addressing from the source conversation (not necessarily the user's real assigned IPs): 100.64.0.10 for the Motorola Razr Ultra 25 (mobile orchestrator, Qwen 3.5 9B), 100.64.0.20 for the Jetson Nano Super (hub, Open-Wiki/vLLM/OmniRoute), 100.64.0.30 for the Rubik Pi 3 (auditor, Gemma 4 E2B, llama.cpp server). Rather than fragile polling REST APIs, the architecture uses a centralized WebSocket router on the Jetson Nano for persistent bidirectional connections, with a connection/keep-alive handshake sent as JSON (event: connection:init, client_id, timestamp, capabilities) and a heartbeat ping every 10 seconds to keep the P2P pipe alive over cellular data.

heading: Task Inference Workflow -- Phase by Phase
content: Phase 1, Meta-Prompt Handshake (phone to Nano): phone STT plus Qwen 3.5 9B build a structured routing meta-prompt sent over a WebSocket stream endpoint, as JSON with session_id, event orchestrator:route_request, intent, meta_prompt text, and context_requirements (source open-wiki:obsidian-vault, query_tags). Phase 2, core injection/processing inside the Nano: the Nano hits the Open-Wiki CLI for roughly a 2KB context slice, sends filtered context plus instructions through OmniRoute to the cloud engine, and receives a proposed script that is not executed yet. Phase 3, Auditor gatekeeper handshake (Nano to Rubik Pi 3): generated code is routed to a dedicated audit WebSocket namespace as JSON with session_id, event auditor:review_request, runtime_environment, proposed_payload (e.g. a bash script), and context_rules. Phase 4, Gemma-4 vision/text audit inside the Rubik Pi 3: the script is piped into Gemma 4 E2B via llama.cpp, optionally appending a desktop screencap via the model's native multimodal layer to confirm the change won't break the visual setup. Phase 5, execution resolution (Rubik Pi to Nano): a structured pass/fail verdict is returned as JSON -- APPROVED includes an execution_token and null error_log; REJECTED includes a descriptive error_log and null execution_token, triggering the Jetson to route the error back through OmniRoute for a zero-cost automated rewrite before re-submission to the Rubik Pi (recursive-loop prevention).

heading: Key CLIs and Utilities Named for This Pipeline
content: Claude Code CLI is suggested to run in an isolated terminal session on the Jetson Nano so the mobile device can offload intensive coding logic while the local executor stays focused on the attached SSD. Fabric CLI is a patterns-based AI orchestration tool (e.g. extract_wisdom, verify_code patterns) suggested to sit on the Rubik Pi for automated validation over incoming text/scripts. LiteLLM is suggested as an internal proxy gateway on the home hub, exposing local models (llama.cpp), private cloud keys, and free cloud endpoints through one OpenAI-compatible API stream. Steampipe CLI is suggested for SQL-style querying of local infrastructure/directories/the 500GB SSD, integrating with the OB1 MCP layer so models can query file metrics like a database. This whole utility list is suggested tooling from the Gemini chat, not confirmed as already installed or working in the user's actual setup.

heading: Relationship to OpenWiki + OB1 + reasoning-bank + Omni Claw
content: This document is the clearest single statement, per the user, of how the three memory-system repos already surveyed (OpenWiki, OB1, reasoning-bank) and the Omni Claw/AESOP vision fit into one real, physical, multi-device deployment. OB1 is named directly and explicitly here as the memory orchestration layer (Nate Jones' OB1/Open Brain, MCP server plus Postgres/Supabase-style memory) running on the home hub. Open-Wiki/LLM-Wiki is named directly as the PDF/Obsidian-graph-to-JSONL compiler feeding the SSD-backed context store -- the same tool covered in the llm-wiki-termux-setup skill package, but here at home-hub scale rather than the on-phone Termux version. The Dual-Agent Talker-Reasoner pattern (Executor/Sandbox plus Query/Talker memory agent) described here is architecturally the same shape as reasoning-bank's success/failure memory-item retrieval concept and Omni Claw's Local Knowledge Synthesis step (the C++ engine pulling skill blocks/context before compiling a meta-prompt) -- all three describe keeping the execution/reasoning layer context-lean while a separate memory/retrieval layer feeds it precise slices on demand. The Rubik Pi 3 Red Agent Auditor is a new capability not previously covered in the OpenWiki/OB1/reasoning-bank/AESOP/Omni Claw docs -- a dedicated code-review/guardrail gate sitting between generation and execution, worth carrying into the eventual integration architecture doc as an additional layer beyond the three repos already scoped. During the conversation the user mentions three repos being woven together -- OB1, Mimir Claw/OpenClaw (recalled as the dual-agent session persistence engine), and Open-Wiki/Model Wiki CLI -- plus a repo in between OB1 and Open-Wiki that could not be recalled by name; this is not resolved in this document and is flagged as an open item if the user wants to identify it later.
